correctness.rationale: Linear substitutions preserve the cube ideal by Frobenius in characteristic three, so symmetric-form congruence diagonalizes Q in the graded algebra. On an active variable the coefficient c_i is absorbed in the length-two chain (1,c_i x_i^2); no square root or agreement of discriminants is needed. Each active variable yields J2[0]+J1[1], with tensor action the sum of multiplication operators, whose cube vanishes. With the notation of RESULT.md §2, J2 tensor J2 has a length-three chain generated by u0v0 and a killed difference u1v0-u0v1. For J3 tensor J2 the difference maps successively to u2v0 and u2v1; in the shared degrees its chain is independent from the one generated by u0v0 since 2 is nonzero, and the six vectors exhaust the space. These graded identities give exactly the three recurrences in §3. Iterating them from (z,1,0) yields 2^(r-1)z^r, 2^(r-1)z^(r-1), and the stated geometric sum; inactive factors contribute T^(n-r). The quotient retains exactly the chain starts. At z=1 its size at positive rank is 3^(n-1)+3^(n-r)2^(r-1), strictly decreasing with rank and smaller than the zero-rank size. For a fixed radical one counts nonsingular symmetric forms on the quotient by summing the two congruence orbit sizes. In even dimension the two factors 1/(q^m-1) and 1/(q^m+1) combine and cancel the corresponding even GL factor; in odd dimension the two orthogonal stabilizers have equal order. This gives the two stated products. Exact hand replay via the recurrence at n=3 gives Hilbert vectors (1,3,6,7,6,3,1), (1,3,5,5,3,1), (1,3,5,4,2) and (1,3,5,4); the independent orbit count at q=3 gives 1,26,234,468. The uploaded checker was inspected but not run; its reported finite cases are not an arbitrary-n proof.

value.rationale: This answers a natural family-wide question not settled by Lefschetz ranks for powers of linear forms: which quotient Hilbert functions and graded multiplication modules occur for an arbitrary single quadratic section? The result distinguishes ranks even by length, gives degree-sensitive information stronger than ordinary Jordan counts, and assigns each stratum an exact frequency. The value is in the classification and its closed formulas, not in recomputing a finite-field table.
